transcript.text: Dropped a cast iron pan on my ceramic hob and there's a crack right across the front left ring. It still heats up. Can I keep using it until I get a new one?

No, you should not keep using it. A crack in the ceramic glass poses a serious safety risk because water or food spills can seep through to the live heating elements underneath, creating a danger of electric shock or short-circuiting. Even though it currently heats up, the structural integrity is compromised and could fail further under heat or weight. You need to stop using that zone immediately and arrange for an engineer to replace the glass cooktop.

Ok, that makes sense. Some pasta water spilled earlier and might have gone into the crack though. Should I turn the hob off at the wall, and is there anything else I should do before an engineer comes?

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. Yes, please turn the hob off at the wall (isolate it at the fused spur or consumer unit) immediately to cut all power. Do not attempt to use it again until an engineer has inspected and repaired it. In the meantime, do not pour water on the crack or try to clean underneath it; simply wipe away any surface spillage gently with a dry cloth if safe to do so without pressing into the crack. The hob must remain isolated until a qualified engineer replaces the glass top.
